newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rwandan refugees accuse militias of massacres.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan refugees accuse militias of massacres.

text.p: Rwandan refugees streamed into Sake at the northern tip of Lake Kivu on Wednesday and some accused Rwandan Hutu militiamen of carrying out large-scale massacres to try to stop refugees leaving their camps.

The refugees arrived from the two camps of Katale and Kahindo north of the city of Goma, which were attacked by Zairean rebels last month apparently in a deliberate attempt to cause panic and flush out the Hutu militiamen.

"I left Katale camp on the 31st of October," said Prosper Ndukireyimenze, from Ruhengeri in northern Rwanda. "Before we left the area around Katale, on the second day, the militias killed a huge group of people."
Other refugees from Katale arriving in Mugunga, near Sake, told a similar tale.
"On the second day of walking we had got outside of the camp, when the Interahamwe killed three or four thousand people, west of the camp," one refugee said.
The reports of massacres could not be independently confirmed because aid agencies were not present in the camps at the time.
The Interahamwe were responsible for carrying out massacres in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda in which up to one million Tutsis and moderate Hutus died.
In the camps in Zaire they effectively used the Hutu refugees as a human shield to defend themselves from Zairean rebels who have put the Interhamwe militiamen and former Rwandan soldiers to flight.
All forces in the complex multi-sided conflict in eastern Zaire have been accused of massacres.
